To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structural adaptation to high salt concentrations of proteins from halophiles that accumulate molar concentrations of salt, is achieved through weakening of the hydrophilic contacts, in particular at level of conserved contacts.

the haloadaptation of proteins through the "salt-in strategy" involves weakening the hydrophobic contacts, in particular at conserved positions, in order to counterbalance the salt-induced strengthening of these interactions."
the haloadaptation of the "salt-in", but not of the "osmote" strategy, is associated with a decrease in the hydrophobic contact network of the conserved residues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms underlying protein haloadaptations.
the structural basis of the halophilic adaptation of proteins and the molecular mechanisms that allow the stabilization of proteins in the presence of high concentrations of salt.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of haloadaptation of proteins and may help the design of proteins stable at high salt concentrations and/or at extreme temperatures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
halophilic proteins are more hydrophilic than their non-halophillic homologues and that this is achieved by weakening of the hydrophilic interactions in the protein interior.
haloadapted proteins are less compact, less hydrophobic and more flexible, but the molecular mechanisms of haloadaptation are still not fully elucidated.
the "salt-in strategy" of halophilic adaptation requires a weakening of the conserved hydrophobics contacts in the protein structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structural adaptation of halophilic proteins is mainly achieved through the weakening of the conserved hydrophobics contacts in the protein structure, and that the "salt-in strategy" is a more effective adaptation mechanism than the "osmotic strategy".
halophiles are able to survive in high salt environments through weakening of their conserved hydrophobics.
halophiles are not only interesting for their extreme habitats but also as models to understand the molecular mechanisms of adaptation and the evolution of proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
haloadapted proteins have a tendency to decrease the strength of the conserved hydrophobics contacts.
haloadapted proteins may be more tolerant to high salt concentrations because their hydrophobic interactions are weakened, in contrast to mesophilic proteins.
the weakening of conserved hydrophilic interactions may be a common strategy of haloadaptation.
